why: Build the string one character at a time: you may add '(' while fewer than n are open, and ')' only while closes < opens. These two rules prune every unbalanced prefix, and trying '(' before ')' yields lexicographic order directly.
hints: Generating all 2^(2n) strings and filtering works for small n but is wasteful. What makes a prefix hopeless?
A prefix is valid iff opens <= n and closes <= opens. Only extend with characters that keep it valid.
Recurse with counts (open, close) and a buffer; add '(' first, then ')'. Output size is the Catalan number C(n), and each string costs O(n).
pitfalls: Copy the buffer when saving a result, or all results alias the same list.
